title: TS streaming: graceful drain, AbortSignal handshake, and ergonomic conversions
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: TypeScript SDK users need predictable semantics when converting between async iterators and WHATWG ReadableStreams, particularly during shutdowns, cancellation, and graceful draining. Current adapters can either drop pending tokens on AbortSignal, leak underlying connections when consumers early-return, or make retry semantics awkward when a stream mid-flight fails. This ticket defines a handshaking pattern + helper primitives that unify semantics, provide an ergonomic developer surface, and enable safe retries and graceful drain on process shutdowns.

Goals:
- Define a clear handshake between consumer AbortSignal and the SDK stream source so both sides can agree on 'drain then close' vs 'abort immediately'.
- Add ergonomic helpers to convert: AsyncIterator <-> ReadableStream without surprising early-return behavior.
- Ensure adapter preserves backpressure and propagates cancellation reasons for observability and retry decisions.
- Add tests, examples, and migration guidance.

Non-goals:
- Full refactor of streaming runtime; this is limited to the public SDK adapters and helpers (thin, well-tested).
acceptance_criteria: Public helpers: toWebStream(asyncIterable, options) and toAsyncIterator(readable, options) implemented and exported from @redwood/sdk/streams
By default an early-return from the consumer signals 'drain-then-close' behavior for streaming completions; immediate abort is opt-in via option { immediateAbort: true }.
Helpers accept an AbortSignal and surface cancellation reason; underlying protocol transport gets a cancellation event so connection can be closed cleanly.

Unit + integration tests cover: backpressure preservation, cancellation propagation, graceful drain on process SIGTERM, retry path where a stream fails mid-generation and SDK surfaces a retryable error with a request-id.
Examples / cookbook added to docs and a short migration note for existing stream adapters.
Design doc + API review comment resolved and final PR merged.
No observable connection leaks in long-running benchmark harness (10k concurrent short streams) after implementation.
testing_plan:
Unit tests for both adapters with a fake transport that emits tokens on set intervals. Tests:
- consumer early-return with immediateAbort=false -> runtime receives 'drain' signal and emits remaining buffered tokens, then close.
- immediateAbort=true -> runtime receives cancel and our fake transport's close called immediately.
- AbortSignal passed to adapter triggers same semantics as explicit return().
- Backpressure: ensure ReadableStream.applyBackpressure by delaying pull resolution; verify number of in-flight tokens never exceeds configured batch size.
- Integration: run the bench harness with 5k short-lived streams, assert no increase in open TCP connections after ramp-down.

Testing infra: extend existing ts-sdk streaming harness (ENG-314159) to add drain-mode scenarios.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind `ts_stream_graceful_drain_v1` (opt-in via SDK env var). 2) Merge adapters + tests. 3) Release canary to internal customers and run bench for 48h. 4) Flip flag for all new SDK versions in the next minor if metrics pass. 5) Add migration note and examples in SDK changelog.
